inputs.text: The court’s finding that Mary Ngechi Ngethe played a central role in buying unsuitable cemetery land for Ksh.283 million points to more than one official’s conduct. When oversight is weak, public procurement can serve insiders instead of people who depend on essential services. The cost falls on the community, including those with the least power to demand answers. Accountability matters, but so does changing the systems that let public money be diverted from public need.
